plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy: bidding higher risks paying more than your value if you win against a bid between your value and your bid, while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since I have no information suggesting otherwise (first round, no history), I will bid exactly my value of $30 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others bid. If I bid exactly my value ($28), I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid, and I always pay less than my value in that case, guaranteeing non-negative profit. Bidding higher risks overpaying (profit could go negative), and bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid my true value.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction), where bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding higher than my value adds risk without benefit, and bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, I will bid exactly my value of $22 to maximize expected profit.
